content:
Jordan Lee: Heads up - alerting from canary deploy v3.1.4 -> 3.1.5. Error spike on model-init decrypt. Noting high 5xxs from the canary pool.
Taylor Kim: on it. Which cluster?
Jordan Lee: us-west-2-canary-3. Service: inference-runtime. Logs show KMS decrypt failures around 14:03 UTC.
Samir Patel: I’m looking at the deploy pipeline. We rotated the KMS key this morning and updated env var REDWOOD_KMS_KEY_ID in the staging pipeline, but looks like the prod canary got the new key id without IAM binding. Might be missing decrypt permission on the role.
Marisol Gomez: @deploy-bot any automated rollback?
deploy-bot: Canary health check failed (10m). Auto-rollout paused. Manual rollback suggested.
Taylor Kim: @oncall-bot page the on-call and create incident channel.
oncall-bot: Paging on-call: priority P1 - Canaries failing due to KMS decrypt errors. Incident channel created: #incident-1764500000.
Jordan Lee: Symptoms: inference processes throw "KMSAccessDeniedException" then crash, BFF 502 to customers. We’re seeing a ~12% increase in overall 5xxs and a small number (≈120 requests) got affected, mostly long-tail low-QPS tenants.
Samir Patel: Fetching IAM trace... run: `aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/redwood-canary-role --action-names kms:Decrypt`
Samir Patel: Result: DENY for key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/abcd-rotated. Missing kms:Decrypt in key policy for that role.
Marisol Gomez: Noted. Does the private deployment fleet also use same key?
Jordan Lee: No, only hosted canary pool uses this key. Dedicated customers unaffected so far.
Taylor Kim: Immediate mitigation: kill the feature flag that routes traffic to canary and promote rollback for the canary instances. Can someone flip the flag? If we kill canary but not rollback code, new instances won't receive that key yet.
Marisol Gomez: I can flip the flag. Doing: `flags kill inference-canary-315`
Marisol Gomez: Done. Traffic now routed away from canary. 60s health check...
deploy-bot: Traffic routing change accepted. Canary traffic reduced to 0%.
Jordan Lee: 5xxs falling back to baseline. Customer-ops, any visible customer-reported incidents?
customer-ops: A small number of customers reported intermittent 502s starting 14:03, we've opened a ticket for affected tenants and attached request ids. No major enterprise SLAs hit yet.
Samir Patel: While flag kills traffic, we should rotate the key policy to add the canary role. Plan: update KMS key policy, re-deploy canary with the existing key id OR revert to previous key id used by canaries. Which is faster?
Taylor Kim: Updating key policy is quick but needs KMS admin approval. Reverting env var in pipeline and re-triggering deploy is slightly faster given approvals. I recommend revert env var for canary to previous key id and then patch KMS policy for the rotated key as follow-up.
Jordan Lee: Agreed. @Samir can you trigger a pipeline rollback to set REDWOOD_KMS_KEY_ID back to `key-legacy-1234` for the canary group? Then we can re-run canary in a controlled window.
Samir Patel: Rolling back canary env var now. CI job started: `ci/release/canary/rollback 1764500000`
Samir Patel: CI success. Canary instances replaced with previous key id, warming up.
deploy-bot: Canary instances healthy. Health checks passed for 2 consecutive minutes.
Jordan Lee: Re-enable canary routing for a small fraction (5%) once stable for 5m.
Marisol Gomez: setting routing to 5%
Marisol Gomez: Done. Metrics: no 5xx spike on that slice.
Taylor Kim: Next steps / postmortem items: 1) Update KMS key rotation runbook to include automated IAM policy update or a pre-rotation checklist. 2) Make env var rollout in pipeline require a migration gate for keys (explicit IAM binding verified). 3) Add a smoke test that attempts KMS decrypt as the canary role during canary promotion. 4) Notify affected customers with timeline.
Jordan Lee: Assign owners: Samir -> KMS policy and runbook, Marisol -> pipeline gating changes, Taylor -> smoke test and monitoring alert. Customer-ops will send customer communication.
customer-ops: Sending updates to affected tenants: initial notification sent with mitigation steps and ETA for root cause timeline.
Taylor Kim: Closing incident channel after follow-up tasks are scheduled. I'll open a postmortem with timeline + action items.
Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone. Leave this thread pinned to #eng-releases for the postmortem link once available.
Marisol Gomez: Pinging for on-call handoff: I’m handing off to Taylor at 15:00 UTC — current state stable.
Taylor Kim: Acknowledged. Taking over on-call.
Jordan Lee: Incident closed (mitigated). Will keep it as TTR incident until postmortem published.
